Subject: Renewal proposal: 24-month ramp + co-term and staged burst credits

Hi Samir / team,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Per our conversation I put together a streamlined renewal approach that addresses your elasticity needs while smoothing unit economics across Q1/Q2 next year. High level:

- Term: 24 months (co-term with current enterprise agreement)
- Capacity ramp: 50% baseline Year 1 Q1, 75% Year 1 Q3, 100% Year 2 — with staged burst credits for peak months
- Pricing: blended unit price with a 7% step-up at the start of year 2 (reflects reserved capacity discount year-over-year)
- True-up window: quarterly 30-day true-ups (we can move to 90-day on request)
- Auto-renew: annual auto-renew with 60-day opt-out; any changes to committed capacity must be confirmed in the opt-out window

I attached a quote (PDF) and a one-page ramp schedule. Two optional levers we discussed: frontloaded credits to cover initial burst months (reduces overage risk) or a larger reserved pool with a smaller per-token price.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm preferred true-up cadence (30 vs 90 days)
2) Confirm whether you want frontloaded burst credits vs a larger reserved bucket
3) If OK, I’ll send a cleaned amendment for signature with suggested billing cadence (annual or quarterly invoice)

Attachment: 20260923-Driftly-Renewal-Quote-v2.pdf (pdf, 3 pages)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,

Folks — forwarding Samir's questions + their internal timeline. Key asks: invoice cadence options, 30 vs 90-day true-up flexibility, and whether frontloaded credits are refundable.

My suggested approach:
- Offer invoicing flexibility: annual prepay (5% additional discount) or quarterly billing (standard pricing). Monthly only for overage customers — avoid monthly recurring invoices for reserved capacity.
- True-ups: default to quarterly 30-day true-up but offer a 90-day true-up as an opt-in for the year if they accept a slightly higher unit price (we can quantify).
- Frontloaded credits: non-refundable but consumed first; if they want refundable credits treat as a prepayment with explicit refund rules (requires finance sign-off).

I'm attaching a quick decision matrix I put together to show sensitivity (Decision-Matrix-credits.xlsx). If we agree internally, I'll send a revised amendment with three options (A: frontloaded credits + annual prepay, B: larger reserved pool + quarterly billing, C: 90-day true-up + no frontload).

Thoughts?

Thanks,
Jasmine
